core_obligations: Identify the first two formulations with the definition and two more with parts (2) and (1) of the equivalence lemma, and note that the two-step covering condition follows (proof lines 7501-7509).

Show the square condition is equivalent to the property: one direction is clear, and in the other the property transfers to the composite of the square by clause (1) and then to the middle arrow by clause (4) (proof lines 7511-7517).

Show the surjective square condition implies the property: the composite of the square has the property by clause (3), and the surjective first arrow is an etale covering, so clause (1) returns the property to the original morphism (proof lines 7517-7524).
difficulty_reason: For a property of morphisms of schemes which is etale local on the source-and-target, the lemma collects seven equivalent formulations: the property itself, the existence of etale local models, the pullback condition along every etale commutative square, the same for one surjective such square, the two etale-covering conditions on the target and on the source, and the two-step covering condition (statement lines 7468-7499). The proof pairs the formulations off: the first two are part of the definition, two more are parts (2) and (1) of the equivalence lemma, the two-step condition follows because the property is now known to be equivalent to both one-step conditions, and the remaining square condition is handled in both directions by applying clause (1) to transfer the property to the composite and clause (4) to descend it, with the surjectivity of the first component turning the single arrow into an etale covering for the converse (proof lines 7501-7524). The claim is H2: no new construction, but seven formulations must each be routed to the correct clause of the definition, and the route is written out for every one of them.
